title: kg_sync.forge_outage takes any parenthesised 5xx number in the push output for a forge outage, so a push-rule refusal that prints '(500)' is retried six times
goal: kg_sync.FORGE_OUTAGE matches only an HTTP 5xx status of the forge (GitLab's 'Internal API error (5xx)', 'returned error: 5xx', an HTTP/x 5xx status line or a 5xx status text), never a bare parenthesised number, so a gate or push-rule refusal that prints '(500)' is not retried and the 503 outage still is

run:
import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kg_sync as k
r=[k.forge_outage("remote: gate: commit message longer than the limit (500)\n ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined)"),k.forge_outage("remote: GitLab: Internal API error (503)\n ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> main (pre-receive hook declined)")]
print("forge_outage (push-rule 500, real 503):",r);sys.exit(0 if r==[False,True] else 1)

notes: SP-z3hyk4eh review gap 2 (S3), on ST-6qusz4km: _tools/kg_sync.py:92 FORGE_OUTAGE's \(5\d\d\) matches any parenthesised 5xx number; bounded (6 tries, about 60 s of pauses), nothing lost.
